title: Vintage Gibson Les Paul Special Value Guide By Year
description: Vintage Gibson Les Paul Special values by year, including TV Yellow originals and 1970s reissues, with condition notes and photos from my guitar archive.
h1: Vintage Gibson Les Paul Special Value Guide
alt: Front of a TV Yellow single-cutaway Les Paul Special with two black P-90 covers

faqs.q: What Is A Vintage Gibson Les Paul Special Worth?
faqs.a: The existing site reference for a clean original 1955 to 1959 TV Yellow Special is $13,000 to $21,000. A 1959 cherry Special has an $8,000 to $15,000 reference. The annual table separates later guitars, and the pricing note explains the condition and source behind the ranges.

faqs.q: Is A TV Model The Same As A TV Yellow Special?
faqs.a: No. The TV Model belongs to the one-pickup Junior family, while the Special has two P-90 pickups. TV Yellow is also a finish on the Special. I identify the model before applying a price range.

faqs.q: Why Is There No 1975 Les Paul 55 Row?
faqs.a: The 2025 published reference lists Les Paul 55 production in 1974 and from 1976 onward. The table follows those periods through 1979. A guitar described as a 1975 example needs its actual model and date checked individually.

faqs.q: Does Each Year Have Its Own Independent Sales Sample?
faqs.a: No. Each covered production year has a row, but several rows share an era reference. The pricing note explains the shared references. Repeating a range doesn't claim a separate set of same-year transactions.

faqs.q: How Does A Headstock Repair Affect Value?
faqs.a: A repaired Special needs comparisons with similar repairs and originality. The quality and extent of the work affect the result. I don't apply one automatic percentage to every repaired guitar.

faqs.q: Does A Refret Make A Special Nonoriginal?
faqs.a: A quality refret preserves the all-original classification of an otherwise original guitar under this site's grading approach. It removes museum-quality status. Neck reshaping and fingerboard replacement are different alterations.

faqs.q: Should I Restore The Guitar Before An Appraisal?
faqs.a: Send photographs of its present condition first and keep any removed original parts. I don't need you to polish the finish, reinstall hardware or disturb the wiring before an initial review.
